data.name: Chandaniht
data.gender_notes: Chandaniht is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Chandaniht is derived from the Arabic and Urdu words 'Chand' meaning moon and 'Aniht' meaning night. It represents the beauty and tranquility of the moonlit night. The name Chandaniht carries the meaning “Moonlight” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu. Parents who choose Chandaniht usually hope their child will grow to embody moonlight and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: The name Chandaniht holds spiritual significance in Islam as it is believed to bring peace and calmness to the mind and soul. It is also believed to represent the beauty and grace of the divine.
data.etymology: Chandaniht belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Moonlight.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Chandaniht total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: The name Chandaniht holds significant cultural significance in various Islamic communities, especially those from Pakistan and India. It is believed that the night sky holds a deep spiritual and symbolic meaning in Islamic culture. The sight of the moon during the various Islamic months such as Ramadan, Shawwal, and Muharram holds great cultural significance. The name Chandaniht is a reminder of the beauty and peace that can be found during the moonlit night, providing a sense of comfort and nostalgia.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Chandaniht can be traced back to verses in the Holy Quran and Hadiths. In Surah Al-An'am, verse 58, Allah (SWT) says, "It is He who raised amongst the beasts some as a sign: you have in them sacred law from Us." Among these animals are mentioned the Cow and the She-Camel. However, Allah (SWT) also mentions the moon, "And indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the succession of the night and the day, and the ship which sails in the sea with that which is of use to mankind and creatures which He has scattered therein [is a sign] therein for people who believe." (Quran, 31:34). The moon is also mentioned in the hadiths, emphasizing its importance, such as the Hadith of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) concerning the importance of the night sky and the stars, "Allah has seventy Thousand nights, but He has made the nights and the days equal for your benefit...and He has written the Laws of the Night in the Larterra of the sky..." (Sunan At-Tirmidhi). The name Chandaniht reminds us to pause and appreciate the beauty of Allah (SWT) in the natural world around us, offering a daily reminder of the grandeur of the Creator and the intricacy of His creation.
